blocks.md: Administrative earnings records kept by the US Social Security Administration (SSA), built from employers' W-2 filings for every worker with a Social Security number.

- **All wage earners** in the US with a Social Security number — not a sample.
- **No top coding**: earnings are recorded in full, so changes at the 99th percentile and above are visible.
- Panel structure: the same person can be followed across years and across employers.

blocks.title: Beyond the lecture
blocks.md: Uncapped W-2 earnings are available from 1978. Access is restricted to approved projects, so most researchers see only published tabulations — for example Song, Price, Guvenen, Bloom and von Wachter, "Firming Up Inequality" (2019), which links workers to firms.
The research extract used for worker-level trade studies is a 1% random sample of US workers. For each worker and year it records:

| Good for | Weak for |
| --- | --- |
| The very top of the earnings distribution | Hourly wages — no hours data |
| Long panels of individuals and firms | Education and other worker characteristics (very limited) |
| No sampling or survey response error | Self-employment and informal earnings |
| Comparing with top-coded surveys | Open access — tightly restricted |

Survey sources such as the [Current Population Survey (CPS)](note:current-population-survey-cps) observe education and hours but suffer from [Top Coding](note:top-coding) and [Classical Measurement Error](note:classical-measurement-error). Tax records such as [IRS Individual Tax Data](note:irs-individual-tax-data) are also uncapped but measure tax-unit income rather than individual earnings.

- [Top Coding](note:top-coding) · [Percentile Ratios](note:percentile-ratios)
